correctness.rationale: Odd order makes inversion fix only the identity, so the center is trivial and distinct reflections never commute. Rotations commute with one another. For a nonidentity rotation x and reflection r_a, the generated subgroup is Dih(<x>), so adjacency occurs exactly when <x> is proper. For two reflections, their product is ab⁻¹ and the generated subgroup is Dih(<ab⁻¹>), giving the stated Cayley adjacency. Degree and edge formulas follow by counting. If A is noncyclic, every nonidentity element is a non-generator, producing the complete join; if A is cyclic, generators are precisely the unit differences. Fresh independent group enumeration for C3, C9, C15, C3×C3, C3×C5 and C5×C5 reproduced centers, every pair adjacency, degrees and the formula 2|E|=3|A|b(A).

final_claim: For every nontrivial finite abelian odd-order kernel A, the non-commuting, non-generating graph of Dih(A) is completely determined by the generators of A: generator rotations are isolated, non-generator rotations join every reflection, the reflection graph is Cay(A,S) on the non-generators, the edge count is 3|A|b(A)/2, noncyclic kernels give an order-only complete join, and the active graph otherwise has diameter two.
limitations: Odd kernel order is essential; even-order kernels have central involutions and commuting reflection pairs.
Only generalized-dihedral groups are covered, not arbitrary Frobenius groups.
